result.narrative:
Boeing sits at a 66.8 score in the High Risk band, driven 65% by payment experience and 35% by news. The payment side shows a single $500k invoice under policy TCI-EX-2026-0001 that is 45 days past due against 60-day terms, a clear step up from the only prior resolved case (3 days late in June 2026). The news side is dominated by a severity-4 "leaves open possibility of more layoffs" Reuters headline from 3 days ago, sitting on top of a well-corroborated 5% commercial-workforce cut announced November 9 and covered by Reuters, WSJ, CNBC and the New York Times, alongside secondary negatives on deliveries, FAA/DOT scrutiny, production delay to late 2027, and a weaker free-cash-flow outlook; several unrelated positive items (new orders, backlog growth, contract wins) did not offset the risk signals because they carry zero severity.

The buyer lands in High Risk because both inputs point the same direction: a deteriorating, if not yet contract-breaching, payment pattern combines with a cluster of credible operational-distress news (mass layoffs, production slippage, regulatory audit) to push the weighted score to 66.8, implying a PD of 0.6395. The adjudicator agreed with the band but flagged caveats: the specific "more layoffs" story is headline-only and single-sourced even though the underlying layoff announcement it builds on is multi-outlet corroborated, and the 45-day-overdue invoice is still inside the 60-day contractual term, with the "deteriorating trend" label resting on just one prior data point.

The recommended limit action is to reduce the TCI-EX-2026-0001 export limit from $9,000,000 to $3,518,374, bringing expected loss from $4,143,960 down to $1,620,000 and aligning exposure with the insurer's 25% PD appetite threshold against the current 0.6395 PD.

A move down to Watch would need the score to fall by 16.8 points below the current level, which would come from the overdue invoice being settled and the payment trend normalizing, and/or the layoff and production-delay news aging out of relevance (news has a 365-day half-life) without fresh severity-4 events. Conversely, any escalation — the invoice crossing the 60-day contractual term unpaid, a new round of confirmed layoffs or production cuts, or additional severity-4 news — would reinforce the current High Risk placement and the case for the reduced limit.
